question: Should Oracle expose a supported command that creates a completed persistent browser session from a user-supplied ChatGPT conversation URL before that conversation is verified by a browser run?
rationale: This is a new public browser/session-state capability rather than a repair to an established contract, and maintainers must decide whether its delayed verification and user expectations fit Oracle's product boundary.

options.title: Accept the manual-import workflow
options.body: Keep the command after the contributor supplies redacted proof that import and the first follow-up preserve the existing fail-closed safeguards.

options.title: Keep manual conversations outside session storage
options.body: Decline the new persistent-session entry point and continue requiring Oracle-created browser sessions for follow-up.

recommendation.title: Accept the manual-import workflow
recommendation.body: Keep the command after the contributor supplies redacted proof that import and the first follow-up preserve the existing fail-closed safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository-specific browser workflow policy and product ownership make steipete the best available decision route.
